figures.Vis22-ex: Exercise structures: Short Q2(c) cyclohexane to cyclohexene scheme and Q2(d) the four C4H10O alcohols A-D (PDF page 99). Original figures archived as c12-chem-ch22-fig-ex-q2c-synthesis and c12-chem-ch22-fig-ex-q2d-isomers (drawn for this lesson after the printed figure; not the textbook's picture). Each is placed after its question. 'cyclohexannol' is drawn as cyclohexanol and B as butan-2-ol (the print gives C5H12O); both are in Book correction boxes.

findings: Solved 2026-10-30 on the owner's request (exercises book by book, in Practice): Chapter 22 (Hydroxy Compounds) exercise as printed on PDF 98-100 (printed pages 95-97), in the book's words and order.

Counts: Q1 ten MCQs (I-X; VIII prints only options a-c), Q2 five short-answer questions (a with parts i, ii, iii, v; b i-iii; c i-iii in one self-check each; d as a lead paragraph plus five self-checks i-v; e), Q3 six constructed-response questions (I-vi), Descriptive Questions Q4-Q7 (four); all solved in English and Roman Urdu. Structures described in words in the answers; the printed structures of Q2(c) and Q2(d) are drawn (see the 2026-11-11 note).
The book prints no answer key. MCQ keys worked out: I d, II d, III b, IV b, V a, VI c, VII a, VIII c, IX c, X a.

Book corrections (kept as printed, Book correction box after the item): MCQ VIII stem ends 'it gives m-bromophenol?' and has only three options (answer 2,4,6-tribromophenol); Q2(a) sub-parts numbered i, ii, iii, v (iv missing); Q2(c) scheme label 'cyclohexannol' misspelt and stage 1 needs light; Q2(d) structure B is printed as CH3CH2C(CH3)2OH, C5H12O (2-methylbutan-2-ol), not a C4H10O isomer (butan-2-ol probably meant), answers give both readings.

Doubtful: MCQ X (key review 2026-10-31): key (a) is correct as printed: Br2 and NaOH give the haloform reaction with propan-2-ol (bromoform, a heavy oily liquid) and none with propan-1-ol; acidified K2Cr2O7 turns green with both. Not a book error, so the Book correction box was removed; the explanation notes that I2/NaOH (iodoform, Chapter 23) is the more common form of the test. Q2(e): A and D both give a single alkene (2-methylpropene); A is given as the answer, D noted. Q2(c)(i) stage 2 reagent (aqueous NaOH) is not printed in the question.

Beyond the chapter (labelled): Q3(iv) distilling off the aldehyde as it forms. Q2(b) and Q6 use Chapter 24's diazotisation and coupling (4-hydroxyazobenzene) and the corrected Chapter 22 hydrolysis step (water, not NaOH). Q2(a)(ii) further oxidation to propanoic acid follows MCQ V's ethanol to ethanoic acid. Q3(v) iodo substitution uses KI with H3PO4 by analogy with the book's KBr/H2SO4 method and its note that H3PO4 is preferred for iodoalkanes.

Comparison answer Q5 carries a two-column table (phenol | benzene). Draft for the academic review. (No figures were added at first; the printed exercise structures are drawn since 2026-11-11, see that note.)

2026-11-11 figure pass (owner: every figure as printed): the scheme of Short Question 2(c) and the structures of 2(d) are drawn and shown after their questions in both languages; the verbal stand-ins are removed.
